From 9648f1c3739505557d94ff749a4f32192ea81fe3 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Vinay Belgaumkar <vinay.belgaumkar@intel.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Feb 2022 10:15:04 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] drm/i915/guc/slpc: Correct the param count for unset param

SLPC unset param H2G only needs one parameter - the id of the
param.

Fixes: 025cb07bebfa ("drm/i915/guc/slpc: Cache platform frequency limits")

Suggested-by: Umesh Nerlige Ramappa <umesh.nerlige.ramappa@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Vinay Belgaumkar <vinay.belgaumkar@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Umesh Nerlige Ramappa <umesh.nerlige.ramappa@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Ramalingam C <ramalingam.c@intel.com>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20220216181504.7155-1-vinay.belgaumkar@intel.com

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/gt/uc/intel_guc_slpc.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/gt/uc/intel_guc_slpc.c
index 13b27b8ff74e..ba21ace973da 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/gt/uc/intel_guc_slpc.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/gt/uc/intel_guc_slpc.c
@@ -110,7 +110,7 @@ static int guc_action_slpc_unset_param(struct intel_guc *guc, u8 id)
 {
 	u32 request[] = {
 		GUC_ACTION_HOST2GUC_PC_SLPC_REQUEST,
-		SLPC_EVENT(SLPC_EVENT_PARAMETER_UNSET, 2),
+		SLPC_EVENT(SLPC_EVENT_PARAMETER_UNSET, 1),
 		id,
 	};
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/gt/uc/intel_guc_slpc.c`**
   - The function `guc_action_slpc_unset_param` was modified to change the second argument of the `SLPC_EVENT` macro from `2` to `1`. This change reflects that the SLPC unset parameter H2G only requires one parameter, which is the ID of the parameter being unset.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `intel_guc_slpc.c` directly addresses a bug related to the parameter count for the SLPC unset operation. By correcting the parameter count from `2` to `1`, the patch ensures that the function correctly aligns with the intended functionality, as indicated by the fix reference to a previous commit (`025cb07bebfa`). This change is part of a broader effort to ensure that the SLPC functionality operates correctly, as suggested by the review and suggestions from other developers.

Here is the commit message:
drm/i915/guc/slpc: Correct the param count for unset param

SLPC unset param H2G only needs one parameter - the id of the
param.

Fixes: 025cb07bebfa ("drm/i915/guc/slpc: Cache platform frequency limits")

Suggested-by: Umesh Nerlige Ramappa <umesh.nerlige.ramappa@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Vinay Belgaumkar <vinay.belgaumkar@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Umesh Nerlige Ramappa <umesh.nerlige.ramappa@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Ramalingam C <ramalingam.c@intel.com>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20220216181504.7155-1-vinay.belgaumkar@intel.com

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by an incorrect assumption in the parameter count for the SLPC unset operation, where it was mistakenly set to require two parameters instead of the correct one, which is the ID of the parameter to unset. This misconfiguration could lead to improper handling of the unset request, potentially causing failures in the SLPC functionality.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int guc_action_slpc_unset_param(struct intel_guc *guc, u8 id)
 {
 	u32 request[] = {
 		GUC_ACTION_HOST2GUC_PC_SLPC_REQUEST,
-		SLPC_EVENT(SLPC_EVENT_PARAMETER_UNSET, 2),
+		SLPC_EVENT(SLPC_EVENT_PARAMETER_UNSET, 1),
 		id,
 	};
 
 	return intel_guc_send(guc, request, ARRAY_SIZE(request));
 }

```c

```
Reason:
The parameter count for the SLPC unset operation was incorrectly set to 2, which implies that the function expected two parameters instead of one. This misconfiguration could lead to improper handling of the unset request, potentially causing failures in the SLPC functionality.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
SLPC_EVENT(SLPC_EVENT_PARAMETER_UNSET, 1),
```
Reason:
The patch corrects the parameter count to 1, which aligns with the requirement that only the ID of the parameter to unset is needed. This change ensures that the SLPC unset operation is handled correctly, preventing potential failures in functionality.
